ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $BE$ bisects $\angle ABC$, and $AE\perp BE$ at point $E$. The area of $\triangle BCE$ is $2$. What is the area of $\triangle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Extend AE to intersect BC at D, \\
$\because$ BE bisects $\angle ABC$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABE=\angle DBE$, \\
$\because$ $AE\perp BE$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle AEB=\angle DEB=90^\circ$, \\
In $\triangle ABE$ and $\triangle DBE$, \\
$\begin{array}{c}
\angle ABE=\angle DBE\\
EB=EB\\
\angle AEB=\angle DEB
\end{array}$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ABE\cong \triangle DBE$, \\
$\therefore$ $AE=ED$, \\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\triangle ABE}={S}_{\triangle DBE}$, \\
${S}_{\triangle ACE}={S}_{\triangle DCE}$, \\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\triangle ABC}=2+{S}_{\triangle CBE}=\boxed{4}$

Because BE is the angle bisector of ∠ABC, the reflection of ray BA about BE coincides with ray BC, so D lies on BC. method.method_draft: Use a reflection construction. First read the diagram as triangle ABC with B and C on the lower side, A above, E inside, and segments AE, BE, CE drawn; AE is perpendicular to BE and BE is the angle bisector at B. Reflect point A across line BE and call its image D. Since BE bisects angle ABC, the reflected ray BA coincides with ray BC, so D lies on BC; since AE is perpendicular to the mirror line BE, points A, E, D are collinear and AE = ED. Then triangles ABE and DBE have equal areas, and in triangle ACD the segment CE is a median to AD, so areas ACE and DCE are equal. Therefore the part of triangle ABC outside triangle BCE, namely ABE + ACE, equals DBE + DCE, which is exactly triangle BCE. Hence area ABC = 2·area BCE = 4.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates. From the figure, take BE as a horizontal axis with B at the origin and E on the positive x-axis. Because AE is perpendicular to BE, write E = (e,0) and A = (e,h). Since BE bisects angle ABC, ray BC is the reflection of ray BA across the BE-axis, so any point C on ray BC has form C = t(e,-h) for some positive t. Compute areas by determinants: area(BCE) = 1/2·e·th, while area(ABC) = 1/2·|det((e,h),(te,-th))| = teh. Thus area(ABC) is exactly twice area(BCE). Given area(BCE)=2, area(ABC)=4.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是三角形 ABC，B 在左下方，C 在右下方，A 在上方；点 E 在三角形内部，连有 BE、AE、CE。题设说明 BE 平分 ∠ABC，且 AE 垂直 BE，已知 △BCE 的面积为 2。
推理：按坐标法，取 BE 为水平 x 轴，令 B=(0,0)，E=(e,0)，其中 e>0。因为 AE⊥BE，所以 A=(e,h)，其中 h>0。又因为 BE 平分 ∠ABC，所以射线 BC 是射线 BA 关于 BE 轴的反射，因此 C 在方向 (e,-h) 上，可设 C=t(e,-h)=(te,-th)，t>0。用行列式算面积：S△BCE=1/2·|det((e,0),(te,-th))|=1/2·teh。S△ABC=1/2·|det((e,h),(te,-th))|=1/2·| -teh-teh |=teh。因此 S△ABC 是 S△BCE 的 2 倍。已知 S△BCE=2，所以 S△ABC=4。
